This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js`, `packages/cli/bin/run.js`, `packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level const object))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via HonoServerPlugin (symbol, a top-level const object))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cli/bin/run-dev.js`, `packages/cli/bin/run.js`, `packages/cli/vitest-tiers.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `242f01a2d4373a769fa3d2ca4e0a9d6f426b6ccf` — the merge of head `89264b0c1ec63f52485b1c6c3b5b957f898e560d` into base `f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 242f01a2d4373a769fa3d2ca4e0a9d6f426b6ccf && git checkout 242f01a2d4373a769fa3d2ca4e0a9d6f426b6ccf
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f 89264b0c1ec63f52485b1c6c3b5b957f898e560d && git checkout -B drift-repro f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f && git merge --no-ff 89264b0c1ec63f52485b1c6c3b5b957f898e560d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f80e2a6dad85950d9ebde910f5123eae49c2781f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Comment-only — holds.** Net diff `aaad682dbc..89264b0c1e`, read in the clone: 7 files, +39 / −27. One new file, `.changeset/20594-cli-bin-provenance-anchors.md` (+12), plus the claim's six files: `bin/run-dev.js` +6/−6, `bin/run.js` +3/−3, `scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` +13/−13, `vitest-tiers.fixtures.ts` +1/−1, `vitest-tiers.ts` +2/−2, `plugin-hono-server/objectstack.config.ts` +2/−2 — 27 lines out, 27 in, and the API file list agrees line for line. Every removed and every added line begins with `//` or ` * ` (each read); no string literal, code token, `describe` or `it` title moves, and the one fixture string adjacent to a change (`name: 'a type-only driver import'`) is a context line. Their routing to #20752 follows the fold `5911936313`.

**(b) The eight anchors — hold; every one is the deciding commit, not a restatement.** Site count 6 + 3 + 13 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 27 matches the body's table. Each anchor's message and diff were read, and each rewritten line was blamed at the base:

- `#14858` → `0c5e97368` (`… exits 2 instead of dying of an uncaught EPIPE (#14858) (#15558)`). It adds `process.stderr.on('error', …)` and its docblock to `run-dev.js` and wrote `:377`. `run.js` `:163`, `:168`, `:220` were written by `b3ef687c04` (#16686), which cites #14858 as the dev-shim precedent — so the deciding commit for what the number named is `0c5e97368`, and the three new wordings ("the crash class commit 0c5e97368 fixed", "carried this listener since commit 0c5e97368", "commit 0c5e97368's card traced on the dev shim") are accurate. Subject `fix(cli): widen check:app-nav-i18n from one app to the declared platform-app population (#17972)`, body `Fixes #17891`; its diff is `check-app-nav-i18n.mjs` +350/−47 plus its changeset, and blame shows it wrote all 13 rewritten lines in that file. Its message carries every decision the nine sites cite: the population criterion (both halves), the per-app invariant with the flat-union negative control, the pass-line diff that came back byte-identical, the verdict naming the app subtree, and one build probe per shell. Deciding.
- `#17759` → `c744c0af3` (new). Subject `fix(platform-objects): translate the Account app's contributed nav_connect_agent in all four locales (#17887)`, body `Fixes #17759`; four locale entries and three provenance rows. Its message states what `:148`, `:238`, `:259` and `:537` cite: "keyed apps.APP.navigation.ID, one namespace per app … apps.setup.navigation.nav_connect_agent never answered for the Account door"; and `ca9d9d361`'s own ablation was a diff of the pass line across this landing, so `:238` is exact. Deciding.
- `#13504` → `44813ba57`. Its subject names PR #14536, but the commit's own diff ties it to the card: "the ACCEPT on #13504 measured 18 of 220 files …", "list stays equal to what the files DO (#13504)", "#13504 fixed that the *.e2e.test.ts name disagrees with behaviour" — so "commit 44813ba57's card" at `vitest-tiers.ts:67` is #13504 by the commit's text. The `vitest-tiers*.ts` files were extracted later by `e88d4df37c` (#14717); the decision stays `44813ba57`'s. Reused from stage 14 (`vitest.config.ts`), same decision.
- `#11332` → `dce5cd4f0` (the ADR-0049 retirement of `capabilities` / `configuration` / `extensions`, PR #13287). It wrote `objectstack.config.ts:19`, including the "(#11332, ADR-0049" text. Reused from stage 16.
- `#10724` → `be21955ba` (`retire the nine dead contributes members … (family: #10724 + #11169) (#12001)`). It wrote `:26`. Reused from stage 16.
All eight are one-parent commits and ancestors of the base (`merge-base --is-ancestor` exit 0 each, clone not shallow); `rev-parse --disambiguate` gives one object each. The ADR / ruling-record rung was checked at the head: a grep of `docs/adr` and `scripts/adr-anchors` for the eight numbers and #14874 hits one file, ADR-0088 line 41, a correction note naming #10724 (history, not the ruling), so no anchor should have gone to the first rung; the control `#7329` hits 1.

**(c) The changeset — owed, `patch` right, prose accurate.** `packages/cli/package.json` at the head: `bin` maps `objectstack` and `os` to `./bin/run.js`; `files` is `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. npm packs a `bin` target regardless of `files`, and the repository's own gate encodes exactly that: `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs:1122` (landed by `d451409d20`, #16988) reads a packed `bin` target as a published surface and names `packages/cli`'s `bin/run.js` as the case. So this diff publishes bytes from a released package, which is the one thing AGENTS.md's changeset rule says `skip-changeset` is not for; `patch` is the level for a change that widens nothing. Two landed precedents take the same shape: `8c1515e847` (#16971), a comment-only `bin/run.js` change with a `patch` "rather than a skip-changeset", and #19123's PR #20226, a `patch` for a docblock citation (ACCEPT `5855952308`). Prose: "Three docblock lines above `bin/run.js`'s `process.stderr` `error` listener" — the docblock spans lines 161 to 238 and the listener is attached at 246; the rewritten lines are 163, 168 and 220. "the commit … that made a failed stderr write non-fatal on the dev shim" is `0c5e97368`'s first squashed title verbatim. "npm packs a `bin` target regardless of `files`" is the package manifest plus the gate above. "Comment only: no command, flag, exit code, error code, export or runtime behaviour changes" is what the diff shows. Nothing in it reads as a behaviour change. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

The declaration pairs `yes` with at least `minor`; `no` — no accept set, export or public face moves, which (a) verifies — pairs with `patch`, and `patch` rather than none because `bin/run.js` ships (①(c)). **Open question — `bin/run.js:225` keeps `#14874`.** For this PR, keeping it is what the claim `5918748154` requires ("stay as they are, unless this stage's history search finds a deciding commit") and what stage 14's ACCEPT ruled for this number. - **C** is excluded by `5914299201`'s own sentence, "a commit that only restates or applies a decision is not it"; `5023630b1` does not even name the number.
- **B** is inside ruling C+D as written. `5749154545` defines D as "runtime strings carry no tracker numbers — the lesson is written into the text" and, in the same sentence, puts "the two shipped tarball lines" under D, first; it refused A because "the two shipped lines keep sending readers to 404"; and the #19123 execution applied exactly that to shipped docblock lines (ACCEPT `5855952308`: "The two lines that ship now state the lesson in words, with no tracker number (D)"). Dropping the number from a shipped comment line whose sentence already states the measured fact is D's form, not a new form the ruling does not name.
- What the texts do not settle is the carrier. The fold `5911936313` describes the form-D stage it moved to #20752 by strings, and this card's remaining stage by comment prose in form C, so a shipped comment line sits in neither description as written; stage 14's ACCEPT separately noted "the `#14874` wording in `bin/run.js` and a gate script: #15809". A as a standing end state is the outcome the ruling refused for shipped lines.
